# Connections You can connect to MongoDB with the `mongoose.connect()` method. ```javascript mongoose.connect('mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/myapp'); ``` This is the minimum needed to connect the `myapp` database running locally on the default port (27017). For local MongoDB databases, we recommend using `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`. That is because Node.js 18 and up prefer IPv6 addresses, which means, on many machines, Node.js will resolve `localhost` to the IPv6 address `::1` and Mongoose will be unable to connect, unless the mongodb instance is running with ipv6 enabled. You can also specify several more parameters in the `uri`: ```javascript mongoose.connect('mongodb://username:password@host:port/database?options...'); ``` See the [mongodb connection string spec](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/connection-string/) for more details.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
